about: MUTATING — delete the forge registry's image versions that no train, no rollback and no cluster can want any more (infra/forge/prune-registry-versions.sh <mode> [keep_trains]). Backlog 9789a827, David 2026-09-17 (the replacement disk was not delivered; 'that order sounds great' — buy the headroom). Measured 2026-09-16: /opt/forgejo/data is 93 GB of the forge's 228 GB disk — the container registry every train pushes a boss:<sha> image to (1–3 GB each, plus boss-ci:<sha> per train) — and nothing pruned the REGISTRY side: prune-registry-tags.lib.sh removes LOCAL docker tags only after the registry holds them (the registry is the rollback path), disk-floor-sweep stops at its floor, and the registry grows ~2 GB per train. Measured 2026-09-17: 1,423 container versions; docker push stores a tag (its one file is the OCI index) plus two untagged sha256 children where the layers live, so the script reads EVERY tag's index through /v2 before classifying and deletes a child only when every tag referencing it goes. THE KEEP SET IS DERIVED, and a half that cannot be derived is a refusal that deletes nothing: the live images (every owner image the cluster runs; deploy/boss in namespace boss required — the watchdog's own read), the rollback target (the converge's last-built stamp the watchdog rolls to by name), the last N landed trains' shas (landed-train-shas.lib.sh over the newest 2N pr-train packets; keep_trains, default 10), latest, everything newer than 24 h, and everything unclassifiable (a tag that is not a sha, an unreadable index, every orphan while any index was unreadable). THE CREDENTIAL is the converge's own docker login for the registry host (the checkout owner's ~/.docker/config.json), used as Basic on the packages API and as a bearer minted at /v2/token for the manifest reads; it rides in a curl config file, never argv, and is never printed. A 403 refuses NAMING THE SCOPE the forge asks for — read:package on the listing, write:package on the first DELETE — a ceremony for David, and the real run stops on that first DELETE. --dry-run derives the keep set, reads the registry and prints the plan (would DELETE / unclassified, by name) and the record; --for-real DELETEs tags first, then children, judged by HTTP code (204 gone, 404 already gone, anything else stops with the count so far on the record). The record is ONE JSON line: kept/delete/deleted/unclassified per package, the keep halves, listed versus the forge's total, and df of the data directory before and after — bytes are not claimed because the packages API declares no sizes and Forgejo's cleanup cron frees blobs later; read df on the packet. Own timeout: one listing page per 50 versions, one manifest read per tag, one DELETE per version. The switch-instance-database shape and process: an explicit per-verb authorization, a precedent for the PROCESS, not a loosened default.
